brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Keep sewing supplies tidy and sorted
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 deep compartments), bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 large compartments) and bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-half-div3 (3 shallow compartments) give 8 separate spaces of different sizes and depths.
3 joint bolts lock the three bases together, 12 end caps close the open sides, and the final check came back clear.
The prop catalogue has no sewing props. Only a marker (prop:1) and a pen (prop:2) stand in the deep bin as stand-ins.

finish.summary:
I built a three-cell sewing organiser in a tight triangle that sits on a table. It has 8 compartments of different sizes across three drop-in bins:
- **(0,0):** 3 full-depth compartments for taller things like scissors, pens and fabric markers.
- **(1,0):** 2 large full-depth compartments for thread spools, a pincushion, tape measures or patterns.
- **(0,1):** 3 half-depth compartments for small things like needles, pins, buttons, bobbins and clips.

I closed every open side with solid end caps and bolted the joints so the bases can't slide apart. The final check came back clear, with no rule errors and no parts overlapping. There are 18 parts in total, and the print estimate is about 1580 g of filament and roughly 36 hours.

The prop catalogue has no sewing items (no thread, scissors or pins). So I only stood a marker and a pen in the deep bin to show what goes where. A tape measure wouldn't fit in the bins' compartments.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
